subject: Follow-up: candidate model ranking, eval artifacts, and temporary safety hold
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@tessera.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: candidate model ranking, eval artifacts, and temporary safety hold

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

What we captured on the call:
- Primary goal: reduce customer-facing hallucination in the credit-decision prompts while keeping latency <= 220ms p95.
- Target workloads: short-form verification (avg 120 tokens) and long-form justification (avg 650 tokens).
- Success signals: A) recall on golden set >= 92%, B) hallucination rate < 2% on sampled prompts, C) p95 token latency within budget.

Candidate models we recommend evaluating first (ranked):
1) redwood/rw-13b-v2 (quantized 8-bit) — best latency/quality tradeoff in our early benchmarks
2) redwood/rw-7b-q4f — very fast, stronger on short prompts
3) open/xxl-21b-8k — highest quality on edge cases, but costlier

Deliverables attached: evaluation pack (eval prompts, golden set, metrics script), short benchmark PDF, and an initial diff CSV that flags areas where recent model builds diverged from your golden set. Links below.

Suggested next steps:
- You: confirm which candidate(s) you want us to prioritize for a 48–72h eval run.
- We: spin up an eval job, share per-model benchmark links + raw outputs, and recommend a canary rollout plan if results look good.
- Contingency: you mentioned concern about last week’s quality dip — if you want us to hold the currently pinned variant while we evaluate, we can do a temporary safety hold (no auto-roll) and snapshot the current model. Please let me know if you want that now.

Quick links: eval pack (Drive), HubSpot deal, preliminary benchmarks.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up today or tomorrow.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com] | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@tessera.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: candidate model ranking, eval artifacts, and temporary safety hold

Thanks Jordan — super helpful. Two quick asks from our side before you run anything: 

1) The production hit last Wednesday (we saw increased hallucinations on a small segment of accounts after an automated model swap). Until we have certs that a candidate won't regress on our golden set, can you put the current production variant into a safety hold / pin so it can't be auto-rotated? We need that for our compliance team.

2) If you run the evals, please include an artifact with token-level diffs vs our golden set and a short summary of any prompt/templating differences you see. We have to present that to our regulators if they ask.

If you can get that in the next 48 hours that would be ideal — we want to move quickly but not at the expense of stability.

—Oliver

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@tessera.ai>
Date: 2026-09-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up — Tessera request: temp pin + diffs (please advise)

Jordan / team — can confirm we can meet Tessera’s ask. Plan and notes below: 

1) Temporary safety hold (pin):
- Action: create a snapshot of current production variant (prod-v1.4.2) and set a manual pin (disable auto-roll policies) for the Tessera tenant.
- Impact: no traffic interruption. Pin takes effect immediately after the snapshot; rollback remains possible.
- ETA: 1 hour from approval.

2) Eval run and artifacts:
- We’ll run a dedicated eval job against the Tessera golden set (attached). Output artifacts: token-level diffs CSV, per-example outputs, and per-model benchmark PDF. See attached candidate-variant-diffs.csv and supporting-benchmarks.pdf.
- Runtime: full pass on your golden set ~6–8 hours on a dedicated runner (we can parallelize to meet 48-hr ask).

3) Canary / monitoring plan (recommended):
- Canary slice: 2% of traffic to candidate variant for 24 hours.
- Metrics to watch: golden-set recall, hallucination rate (automated label heuristics), token p95 latency, user error rate.
- Auto-fallback: if hallucination rate increases >1.5x baseline OR recall drops >3 percentage points, automatic fallback to prod-v1.4.2 triggers.

4) Rollback and roll-forward:
- Rollback: immediate (under 2 minutes) and logged in the Console audit trail.
- Roll-forward: requires canary success and manual approval from Tessera.

Attachments included: candidate-variant-diffs.csv (token diffs), supporting-benchmarks.pdf, tessera_eval_pack_v1.zip (eval prompts + golden set).

Next steps: Jordan — get Tessera approval for the pin now and confirm which candidate(s) to run. Priya — can you confirm we have Dedicated runner time available tonight?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
